mark_split.label: Divide, then set up the form

verification.note: Source: Baby Bullet-Q, Senior Inter Maths-2A (Sri Publishers, Machilipatnam), book p.68 — SAQ chapter 11 Partial Fractions, the 'PQ' practice question printed between answers 103 and 104, which the book gives with its final answer only ([Ans: 1/2 − 1/(50(2x − 1)) − 8/(25(x + 2)) + 27/(25(x − 3))]) and no working — the full solution on this card is OURS, and it reaches the book's printed answer. Printed appearances: none — the practice question carries no year tag. ⚠ THE 1+1+1+1 SPLIT IS OURS, NOT THE BOOK'S — this chapter prints no [N Marks] tags against any answer, only tick boxes. The split is the four moves of the method (set up the form · clear the denominators · find the constants · write the result), one mark each, and the SAME split and the SAME step ids (s1_form, s2_identity, s3_constants, s4_result) are used on all fifteen cards of this unit, deliberately: they are one method over different fractions. For the improper fractions the division lives inside s1_form, and for the (x − 3)³ question the substitution x − 3 = y takes the place of the form. The book's SAQ chapter header carries ★★★ and reads '4 Marks'; that star is the CHAPTER's rank, not this question's. This is a coaching publication, not a TSBIE document, so the split stays unverified until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. Paper position: Maths-2A Section B runs Q11–Q17 at 4 marks each, answer any 5 of 7; Q15 is the Partial Fractions slot (the chapter has no Section A or Section C slot). Not asked at Q15 in any of the five model papers. No two-book check and no board back-test exist for this paper — recorded, not hidden. A back-test against the book's own six papers (the five Model Guess Papers plus the Bullet Model Paper, 199 slot-instances) WAS run on 2026-08-29: all 199 resolved to an authored card, and every one carried the section and marks its slot implies. That is a substitute corpus, not a board paper — it cannot show what the board asks that this book omits. Truth check: putting x = 0 in the identity gives 0 = (1/2)(−1)(2)(−3) + A(2)(−3) + B(−1)(−3) + C(−1)(2) = 3 − 6A + 3B − 2C = 3 + 3/25 − 24/25 − 54/25 = 3 − 75/25 = 0 with A = −1/50, B = −8/25, C = 27/25, so the book's printed answer is confirmed.

recall_prompt: Say how you would resolve x³/((2x − 1)(x + 2)(x − 3)) into partial fractions — name each move in order, starting with what must be done before the form is written.
insider_note: Write the constant 1/2 before the three fractions — the degrees are equal, so the fraction is improper; and fractions with 25 and 50 are expected here: A = −1/50 is correct, not a sign of an error.

steps.label: Divide, then set up the form
steps.margin_note: First mark. Degree 3 over degree 3: improper, and the quotient is the constant 1/2 from the leading coefficients 1 and 2·1·1 = 2. Three different linear factors, so A, B, C over each.

recall.must_convey: That equal degrees make the quotient the constant 1/2, and the form is 1/2 + A/(2x − 1) + B/(x + 2) + C/(x − 3).
accept: the degrees are equal so the quotient is half, then write half plus A over two x minus one plus B over x plus two plus C over x minus three
improper with equal degrees so a constant half comes first and then one constant over each of the three factors
half plus A by 2x minus 1 plus B by x plus 2 plus C by x minus 3
degrees same kabatti quotient half, tarvata A by two x minus one plus B by x plus two plus C by x minus three rasali
write the constant from the leading coefficients and then three fractions for the three linear factors
heard_as: A over two x minus one

steps.why: The denominator expands to 2x³ + …, so x³ divided by it is 1/2 plus a proper fraction. The constant must appear in the form; without it the identity has no solution.
common_mistakes: Writing the three fractions with no 1/2 in front.
Taking the leading coefficient of the denominator as 1 and writing a quotient of 1.

steps.label: Clear the denominators
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Multiply by (2x − 1)(x + 2)(x − 3). The 1/2 keeps the whole denominator; each constant keeps the two factors that are not its own.

recall.must_convey: That multiplying through gives x³ = (1/2)(2x − 1)(x + 2)(x − 3) + A(x + 2)(x − 3) + B(2x − 1)(x − 3) + C(2x − 1)(x + 2).
accept: multiply both sides by all three factors to get x cubed equals half into the whole denominator plus A into x plus two into x minus three plus B into two x minus one into x minus three plus C into two x minus one into x plus two
clear the denominators and the half keeps the whole denominator while each constant keeps the other two factors
x cubed equals half times the denominator plus A B C times the other two factors each
moodu factors tho multiply cheste x cube equals half into whole denominator plus A B C into migatha rendu factors
remove the fractions and keep the half term multiplied by the full denominator
heard_as: B into two x minus one
C into two x minus one

steps.why: The constant 1/2 is a term and is multiplied like every other term. The three products then carry the three constants, each ready to be isolated by one root.
common_mistakes: Giving A the factor (2x − 1) that it sits over.
Writing the identity over x³ but forgetting one of the three products.

steps.label: Find the constants
steps.margin_note: Third mark. Three roots: x = 1/2 for A, x = −2 for B, x = 3 for C. At x = 1/2 the brackets are (5/2)(−5/2) = −25/4, so A = (1/8)(−4/25) = −1/50. Fractions with 25 and 50 are expected here.

recall.must_convey: That x = 1/2 gives A = −1/50, x = −2 gives B = −8/25 and x = 3 gives C = 27/25.
accept: put x equals half to get A equals minus one by fifty, x equals minus two to get B equals minus eight by twenty five and x equals three to get C equals twenty seven by twenty five
the three roots half minus two and three give A minus one fiftieth B minus eight twenty fifths and C twenty seven twenty fifths
A minus one by fifty, B minus eight by twenty five, C twenty seven by twenty five
x equals half pedithe A minus one by fifty, x equals minus two pedithe B minus eight by twenty five, x equals three pedithe C twenty seven by twenty five
three substitutions at the roots give the three constants

steps.why: Each root makes two of the three products and the 1/2 term vanish, leaving one constant. The root of 2x − 1 is 1/2; forgetting that and using x = 1 gives nothing useful.
common_mistakes: Using x = 1 for the factor (2x − 1); its root is 1/2.
At x = −2 computing (−4 − 1)(−2 − 3) as −25 and getting B = +8/25.

steps.label: Write the result
steps.margin_note: Last mark. 1/2 first, then −1/(50(2x − 1)) − 8/(25(x + 2)) + 27/(25(x − 3)). This matches the answer the book prints for its practice question. The result is too long for one box, so the constants are boxed under it.

recall.must_convey: That the fraction equals 1/2 − 1/(50(2x − 1)) − 8/(25(x + 2)) + 27/(25(x − 3)), with the constant 1/2 in front.
accept: the answer is half minus one over fifty into two x minus one minus eight over twenty five into x plus two plus twenty seven over twenty five into x minus three
half first then minus one by fifty two x minus one minus eight by twenty five x plus two plus twenty seven by twenty five x minus three
the constant half comes first and then the three fractions with their signs
final answer half minus one by fifty into two x minus one minus eight by twenty five into x plus two plus twenty seven by twenty five into x minus three ani rasali

steps.why: The constant quotient and all three fractions, with their signs, make the answer. Two of the constants are negative, so two terms are subtracted.
common_mistakes: Leaving out the 1/2 in the final line.
Not checking: put x = 0 in the identity, 0 = 3 + 3/25 − 24/25 − 54/25. If the two sides differ, a constant is wrong.
